AI Tender Review System

A case study in deploying AI for compliance in a regulated environment — companies' tender review

Nasi Li-Purcell

The Problem

Slow and High-Stakes

Manual

Time-consuming

Compliance

What the System Delivers

Traceability

Every parsed clause and every extracted rule carries its exact source: file, page, character span, on-page bounding box.

Auto-detect

A vendor's submission is automatically resolved, read, and checked against the tender's own rules — no manual page-hunting.

Human-in-the-loop

Nothing ships as a silent verdict. Flagged fields get a real Confirm / Reject / Note action, logged with who and when.

System Design — the two stages

One rubric, authored once — evaluated against every vendor

Stage 1 · Rule Extraction
Tender Documents
→
RULE EXTRACTIONparse + author rubric
→
Rule RubricJSON, per schedule
Stage 2 · Rule Evaluation
Vendor 1 Documents
↓
RULE EVALUATIONvendor docs + rule rubric
↓
Verdict
Vendor 2 Documents
↓
RULE EVALUATIONvendor docs + rule rubric
↓
Verdict
Vendor N Documents
↓
RULE EVALUATIONvendor docs + rule rubric
↓
Verdict

Vendor 1 is real, tested end to end. The same rubric is designed to apply unchanged to every other vendor in the tender.

What we actually did for LLM eval

Three Evals, Against Real Data

StepDataset / scriptResult
Parse + Citationtraceability_groundtruth_eval_2.md239/241 resolved · 99.2%
Vision Extractioneval_dataset_20.py20/20 · 100%*
Resolve (semantic search)vendor_check_orchestrator.py12/12 attempted found a real page

*Vision extraction: small, selection-biased sample, near-zero coverage of the messiest tender. Resolve: only 12 of 15 items have anything to look for — the other 3 never attempt resolve at all (physical sample, covered by a sibling rule, or extractor not yet built), not 3 failed attempts. Of those 12, literal title matches are reliable across repeat calls; semantic-only matches have proven non-reproducible (5 identical calls, same input, temperature 0 — found/not-found flipped) — routed to human review rather than trusted blind.
